title: Cynical beliefs about human nature and income: Longitudinal and cross-cultural analyses

publication.publisher_or_container: Journal of Personality and Social Psychology

verification.verification_notes: Metadata confirmed via Crossref API; volume/issue/pagination (110(1):116-132) confirmed 2026-09-24. Abstract read via Europe PMC (PMID 26011659): five studies — two US longitudinal waves (cynical beliefs about human nature predicted lower income nine years later), a German panel study, a Big Five-independent replication, and a 41-country cross-national analysis. Proposed mechanism: cynical individuals avoid cooperation and over-invest in monitoring others. Scope condition: the costs of cynicism were alleviated in contexts of high harm experience or high societal cynicism, so cynicism is not uniformly maladaptive. The record establishes dispositional cynicism as a measurable worldview with consequences, not merely a surface style. Full text not inspected; no passage quoted.
